view: The story has moved from who leads Nvidia to whether Nvidia's reported numbers can be trusted. The beat-and-raise on 2026-11-17 did not stop the fall, and the 2026-11-20 report of an SEC accounting probe took the stock down 14%. On my own 2026-11-15 definition the Commerce remote-access rule fires TB3, and TB2 has become permanent now the board will not reinstate Huang. With two thesis breaks standing and an accounting question that TB1-TB4 do not cover, no ladder should be active. The probabilities are fat-tailed on both sides: there is deep capitulation, but follow-on headlines are almost certain inside the window (testimony requested for Dec 1-3).

probabilities.defs: 2w +/-5%, quarters +/-10%, vs price_at_call 125.53 (Fri 2026-11-20 close, weekend run). next_2_weeks: up = close > 131.81, down = close < 119.25, range between; measured at the close on or before 2026-12-06 (Fri 2026-12-04). this_quarter: close of 2026-12-31; next_quarter: close of 2027-03-31; up = close > 138.08, down = close < 112.98, range between. up + range + down = 100.

evidence.point: SEC. Reuters (2026-11-20, citing two people briefed) reports that SEC enforcement staff are examining potential accounting issues. The start date and the practices involved are unknown. Nvidia did not respond and the SEC declined comment. WSJ reported an SEC investigation on 2026-11-17 without a reason. Press speculation names two areas: revenue reported by customer headquarters rather than billing location (FT: the switch came as Singapore-billed sales neared half of revenue) and the $118B of customer guarantees. This is an enforcement-staff inquiry reported by the press. It is not a Wells notice, a charge, a restatement or a company disclosure.

The export and accounting stories are joining up. Bessent (2026-11-15) questioned whether illicit chip sales boosted earnings, and the speculated SEC focus (where revenue is attributed geographically, Singapore billing) sits on the same Southeast Asia channel as the diversion story. This is the narrative path that matters most. If an official document links the two, TB1 and an accounting break could fire together.

TB3 candidate. The BIS interim final rule 'Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors' was filed 2026-11-16 and took effect 2026-11-19. It requires a license for advanced AI chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and Brazil, and a license for any data center worldwide that gives large compute to China-HQ companies, with 90 days for existing providers. It also rescinds the 2025 AI Diffusion Rule, and China objected. Against my 2026-11-15 test (a material rule that covers existing remote-access or cloud channels AND requires licensing rather than notification), it meets both limbs and is the broader worldwide version, not the narrower Lutnick version I said would not fire.

How material TB3 is remains unquantified, so I flag the doubt rather than hide it. The Q4 guide of $130B (consensus about $124.8B) already assumes zero China data-center compute. China-HQ revenue was $19.7B in FY26, and $2.4B of China Hopper shipped last quarter. A licence requirement is not a denial. The rescinded Diffusion Rule partly offsets it. The guide came the day after the rule was filed, and the slice does not say whether the guide reflects it. The addressable-market cut is real for China-HQ compute bought offshore, but no source puts a number on it.

Leadership. Chair Harvey Jones says the board will not reinstate Huang, although Huang said he would be honored to return. Heidrick & Struggles has been hired, with no timeline. Bessent has publicly urged an outside CEO and a 'dramatic shakeup'. TB2 is now a permanent key-person loss rather than a reversible one. A successor before 2026-12-31 is unlikely, so there is no governance upside catalyst this quarter.

Congress. The House chairs asked for a closed-door interview with Huang on 2026-12-01 and with Nvidia's general counsel on 2026-12-02. Senate Banking asked for Huang on 2026-12-03 and Lutnick on 2026-12-10. The briefing planned for 2026-11-18 did not happen, so these are requests that may slip again. The general counsel request is new and points at the company, not only the former CEO.

TB1 is still NOT fired. DOJ charged Super Micro executives with conspiring to divert AI servers to China, and Supermicro's internal probe found no senior-management involvement. DOJ is reviewing the planned $12.9B Hugging Face purchase, which is antitrust or deal review and not an export finding. No charge, settlement or admission names Nvidia. The Supermicro charge shows DOJ is actively prosecuting the channel, which raises my 2q TB1 odds slightly.

This week's fall was mostly sector-wide. On Friday NVDA fell 14.01% against SOX -10.73%, AMD -13.25% and SPX -3.7%. For the week NVDA fell 22.92% against SOX -17.13% and SPX -8.61%. Last week's damage was company-specific. This week about three-quarters of the move was shared with the sector and AI-repricing headlines (slowing data-center construction, tighter funding). The SEC report explains the Friday excess, not the whole move. Peer weekly data are partial.

TB4 monitor: 0 of 4 falling. Run-rate vs TTM is MSFT +15.9%, GOOGL +28.5%, AMZN +43.6% and META +30.0%. No quarter has been reported since 2026-11-15, so TB4 is NOT fired and NOT on watch. There is no report in news_governance of a guidance cut by any of the four. The AI-repricing story is a narrative risk to TB4, not evidence for it. what_would_change_my_mind: Expected (not a trigger): the window will bring more SEC, testimony and remote-access headlines, and the 2026-12-02 ex-dividend date (immaterial). What matters is the outcome of these events, below.

More bearish (signal): Nvidia confirms an SEC inquiry by 8-K or statement that names revenue recognition, geographic attribution or the guarantees; OR it delays a filing, its auditor resigns, or it discloses a material weakness; OR there is a credible report from the Dec 1-3 sessions that Nvidia knew of the diversion. Any of these before 2026-12-31 moves my this_quarter call toward 28/27/45 and raises TB1 2q odds to about 30%.

More bullish (signal): Nvidia states the SEC inquiry is an informal or narrow request on disclosure presentation with no restatement expected, AND the testimony sessions pass with no new Nvidia-level disclosure. Before 2026-12-31, that moves me toward 42/28/30.

TB3 materiality: BIS licences granted to the large Singapore/Malaysia data-center operators, or a company quantification showing the rule's at-risk revenue is small, before the end of the 90-day window (about 2027-02-17), would support the owner ruling TB3 immaterial. Licence denials or a company estimate of lost revenue keeps it fired.
TB1 fires: a DOJ or Commerce charge, settlement or penalty, or a company admission, naming Nvidia itself (not Supermicro, Megaspeed or Alice Huang) before 2027-03-31.
TB4 WATCH: two or more of MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN/META show a run-rate more than 10% below TTM, or any one guides capex down on its next call. TB4 fires only if two or more guide down.

Price (reachable): a daily close below 119.25 by 2026-12-04 (-5%, 2w reach 41.2%) confirms the accounting discount is still being added. A daily close above 145.71 by 2026-12-31 (about +16%, 6w +10% reach 54.5%, +20% reach 28.2%) means the Friday SEC gap is repaired.
notes_for_chair: TB STATUS (my readings; the chair rules and the owner confirms): TB1 NOT fired. TB2 FIRED (2026-11-12 ruling) and now permanent, because the board will not reinstate Huang; I recommend it stays fired. TB3: I read it as FIRED on 2026-11-19. TB4 NOT fired and NOT on watch (0/4 falling). Any one break pauses all buying, and buying was already paused under TB2, so the TB3 reading costs nothing extra today. It does matter for the un-pause path.

TB3 reasoning. On 2026-11-15 I committed in advance that a rule fires TB3 if it covers existing remote-access or cloud channels AND requires licensing rather than notification, and that the narrower Lutnick version would not fire it. The enacted rule requires licensing, covers data centers worldwide that serve China-HQ firms, and gives existing providers 90 days. It meets my definition. Re-defining after the fact would be moving the goalposts. The honest caveat is the config wording 'materially cut addressable market': no quantification exists yet, the Q4 guide already assumes zero China DC, licences may be granted, and the Diffusion Rule rescission partly offsets the rule. I therefore recommend the chair rule TB3 FIRED (provisional) and put materiality to the owner, with the un-fire test being licence outcomes or a company quantification within the 90-day window.

SEC accounting probe: not covered by TB1-TB4. I recommend the chair ASK THE OWNER whether to add a thesis break, as a proposal only. Suggested wording: 'TB5: Financial-reporting integrity break. Nvidia restates or says prior financials should not be relied on, discloses a material weakness, its auditor resigns or qualifies its opinion, it misses a 10-Q/10-K deadline, or it discloses a Wells notice or SEC enforcement action on accounting.' A press report that staff are 'examining' issues should NOT fire it, which is why it is not fired today; I would put it on WATCH. Why it deserves its own break: every valuation argument (forward P/E of about 8.4, a beat-and-raise, analyst targets) assumes the reported numbers are reliable. TB1-TB4 protect the demand and legal thesis but not the integrity of the numbers.

TB odds (my judgment, not slice numbers). TB1: 2w about 4%, 2q about 22% (was 3%/18%; raised because DOJ has charged the Supermicro channel, the general counsel has been requested, and the export and SEC stories are converging). TB3 materiality confirmed (if the owner wants a stricter test): 2q about 55%. TB4: 2w about 1%, 2q about 8% (was 6%; the AI-funding repricing story raises it slightly, with no capex evidence). Proposed TB5: 2w about 5%, 2q about 15%. Accounting probes usually take quarters to conclude, and the first firm checkpoint is the annual report and its auditor opinion.

How the market usually prices these shocks. A key-person exit is priced mostly in its first days. An accounting probe is different: it removes the market's trust in the earnings base, so cheap multiples stop working as support, and the discount usually lasts until an official document resolves it (a company statement of scope, a clean auditor opinion, or a settlement). Rules are priced in steps at each official document. The remote-access rule was step one, and licence decisions are the next step. Pattern so far: the exit gapped down and partly recovered (Nov 12), the rule took effect quietly (Nov 19), the beat did not help, and the SEC report produced the largest drop (Nov 20). The market is ranking accounting doubt above export rules and the CEO loss.

Noise, next 2 weeks: Bessent or other officials' commentary, candidate-CEO names, Huang's statements about returning, more downgrades or target cuts (one analyst group), new class-action filings, China's ministry objections, Hugging Face deal-review headlines, and whether the testimony sessions are rescheduled. Signal, next 2 weeks: any Nvidia 8-K or statement on the SEC inquiry (and the words used: 'informal', 'subpoena', 'Wells'), credible accounts of what Huang or the general counsel told the committees, any DOJ filing naming Nvidia, senior finance or audit-committee departures, and BIS licence decisions for Singapore/Malaysia operators.

Noise, next 2 quarters: the political argument about the scope of controls, and analyst re-ratings. Signal, next 2 quarters: the auditor opinion and controls language in the annual report, any restatement, the outcome of the SEC inquiry, whether licences are granted or denied by the end of the 90-day window (about 2027-02-17), who becomes permanent CEO (an outsider is a larger strategic change), the outcome of the board investigation, and the hyperscalers' next capex guidance.

LADDER: GOVERNANCE CONDITIONS (proposals only; the owner decides; I never suggest executing orders). (1) While any thesis break stands (TB2 now, TB3 on my reading), no ladder is active, whether old or updated. A committee proposal can be drafted, but it stays dormant. (2) TB2 un-pause needs all of these: the Dec 1-3 sessions (or their replacements) pass with no credible report that Nvidia knew of the diversion; no charge or admission names Nvidia; and a permanent CEO is named or the board gives a credible timeline. (3) TB3 un-pause needs the owner to rule the rule immaterial on evidence (licence grants or a company quantification), not on price. (4) Before any activation, the owner decides whether to adopt the proposed TB5. Even if it is not adopted, I propose a minimum accounting gate: Nvidia has publicly described the scope of the SEC inquiry and there is no restatement, auditor change or material-weakness disclosure. The cleanest clearing event is the annual report with an unqualified auditor opinion (date not in slice). (5) The existing earnings blackout (3 trading days before the late-Feb 2027 print) still applies. (6) If the owner wants a staged route, the narrative-lane view is that the first tranche should wait for the accounting gate rather than for a price level. Price levels and weights belong to technical and the chair.

Before vs after the 2026-11-17 print. Before the print, I said the 2w odds could shift by up to about 10 points depending on the disclosures. After it, the print beat (EPS 2.68 vs 2.47; guide 130B vs about 124.8B) and the stock still fell 4 straight sessions, then fell 14% on the SEC report. My lesson: in this regime the stock is not trading on earnings size, it is trading on governance and on whether the numbers can be trusted. Changes from my 2026-11-15 submission (at 162.85, older thresholds): 2w 35/31/34 -> 37/27/36, this quarter 33/35/32 -> 35/30/35, next quarter 41/28/31 -> 41/24/35, confidence 48 -> 44. On the old thresholds my 2w call has effectively resolved 'down' (125.53 is below 154.71 with a week left); the chair should log that for the lessons file when it is scored.

Cross-domain: the guarantees ($118B maximum against $53.5B cash; BofA estimate $230B) and the D&O cover belong to fundamentals. The sector-wide share of the move and AI-repricing breadth belong to relative_strength and macro (VIX 35.90, Nasdaq's worst week since March 2020). Stale AAII and CNN pages belong to sentiment. sec_filings being stale or partial is the most important gap for this lane and should be re-read before the chair rules.

Pre-mortem: if this is badly wrong in 3 months, the most likely reason is that the SEC matter turned out to be a narrow disclosure-presentation question, the market re-rated a stock at about 8x forward earnings sharply, and the stacked pauses (TB2 + TB3 + a proposed TB5) kept the owner out of the low. The second most likely reason is the opposite: a restatement or a combined export-accounting finding took the stock through 112.98, and my down odds were too low because I leaned on capitulation base rates built from n=4.
